paraphrase_a: There exists at least one swan that is not white.
rationale: Negation outscopes the universal quantifier: ¬∀x(swan(x) → white(x)).

target: All the kids didn't finish their homework.
paraphrase_a: Not all of the kids finished their homework.
paraphrase_b: Every single kid failed to finish their homework.
rationale: Ambiguous: surface scope ∀¬ and inverse scope ¬∀ are both available.

paraphrase_a: There are many people who dislike cilantro.
rationale: many > not: a substantial number have the property of not-liking; does not imply few like it.

target: She didn't read every book on the list.
paraphrase_a: There is at least one book on the list she did not read.
paraphrase_b: She read none of the books on the list.
rationale: ¬∀ reading is the dominant one; the ∀¬ reading is pragmatically marked here.
